documents.title: Flock request #2112 harvest: Dunwoody renewal, operations, and native-record surfaces
documents.summary: Harvests mature first-party Dunwoody evidence from the Flock backlash request into the canonical Flock corpus while keeping the Targeted Victory, SixAM Strategies, and West Shore Strategies retainer/astroturf allegations unresolved pending native engagement records.

gaps: The native February 6 calendar production and February 12 meeting invitation, headers, attachments, and surrounding correspondence remain unresolved.
No primary contract, SOW, invoice, payment, or attributable work product reviewed here establishes that Flock retained Targeted Victory, SixAM Strategies, or West Shore Strategies.
The current exact executed 2026 Dunwoody Flock agreement bundle and its incorporated terms require direct contract-level reconciliation.
Account-level RTCC/Flock/Fusus access, audit logs, camera-level inventory, and actual external-sharing configuration remain unresolved.

data.question: Which mature Dunwoody findings from request #2112 are established strongly enough to materialize without promoting the unresolved PR-firm/astroturf allegations?
data.method: Harvested first-party Dunwoody operational, transparency, and records-custody evidence accumulated in request comments while retaining secondary PR-firm meeting claims only as unresolved targets.
data.framework: Deployment state, renewal controversy, platform operation, records custody, PR-firm meeting lead, contractual engagement, paid influence, and causal effect are separate evidence states.
data.scope: Dunwoody Flock-powered RTCC, continued 2026 operational state, public transparency/retention surface, and native municipal records/payment recovery paths relevant to the crisis-PR allegation.
findings: Dunwoody Police publicly identifies its Real Time Crime Center as Flock-powered; the center was unveiled in August 2024 and combines LPR and other camera/response feeds.

The current Dunwoody Flock transparency surface reports a 30-day retention setting and exposes a large camera surface; this is a current public configuration statement, not a historical guarantee for every period or device.

City of Dunwoody records infrastructure provides native recovery surfaces for agendas, agenda packets, minutes, videos, approved contracts and agreements, open-records productions, contract administration, Open Checkbook data, and monthly financial/check-register records.

Those municipal systems provide a deterministic evidence route for testing the Targeted Victory, SixAM Strategies, West Shore Strategies, Stagwell, or related professional-services allegations through contracts, SOWs, invoices, purchase orders, payments, reimbursements, correspondence, and work product.

Dunwoody's June 2026 police operations material documents active RTCC/remote-camera use and a Drone-as-First-Responder assist after the April renewal controversy, supporting classification of Dunwoody as a contested-but-continued/renewed Flock deployment rather than a cancellation case.
Continued operation after the controversy does not establish that an outside PR firm caused the renewal decision, had platform access, or produced paid local advocacy.
The reported February 12 RTCC-tour meeting and outside-firm attendee list remain an attributed open-records lead until the native calendar production and related records are independently recovered.
conclusions: Dunwoody is a verified active/continued Flock case within the 2026 backlash ledger, not a completed cancellation/offboarding case.

The strongest next step for the PR-firm allegation is no longer generic web research; it is native City Clerk, open-records, procurement, accounts-payable, and check-register recovery joined to Flock-side records.
Nothing in the mature evidence harvested here supports canonizing a Targeted Victory, SixAM, or West Shore retainer, astroturf campaign, paid media placement, or causal influence on the council vote.
recommendations: Recover the original February 6 calendar item for the February 12 RTCC tour, including headers, invitees, attachments, and surrounding February 6-12 correspondence.

Search Dunwoody contracts, SOWs, purchase orders, invoices, Open Checkbook, monthly check registers, reimbursements, and vendor records for Targeted Victory, SixAM Strategies, West Shore Strategies, Stagwell, Flock, and related legal entities.
Recover the executed 2026 Flock agreement bundle and compare its exact terms against older/public standard terms rather than back-projecting current web terms.
Recover account-level RTCC/Flock/Fusus audit, sharing, and camera inventory evidence separately from the PR/public-affairs investigation.
counterarguments: An outside communications professional appearing on a reported meeting invite does not establish a paid engagement, meeting substance, or resulting influence tactic.
A renewed or operational Flock deployment after public controversy does not establish that outside communications activity caused the decision.
limitations: This bounded harvest intentionally excludes unverified retainer, astroturf, paid-placement, and causal-influence claims.
It materializes mature Dunwoody first-party evidence while the broader national cancellation/offboarding and PR-network request remains open.
unresolved: Did Flock retain Targeted Victory, SixAM Strategies, West Shore Strategies, or related firms for Dunwoody or the broader backlash response?
What did the February 12 Dunwoody RTCC meeting actually discuss and produce?
What executed 2026 contract terms governed Dunwoody's data, publicity, hardware, termination, and access state?
Which accounts and agencies actually accessed or shared Dunwoody RTCC/Flock data during the relevant period?
